title: AnomalyGFM: Graph Foundation Model for Zero/Few-shot Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Graph anomaly detection identifies abnormal nodes that differ from most nodes in a graph.

gap.claim: Existing generalist graph models struggle to generalize to graph anomaly detection because abnormality patterns are infrequent, irregular, and heterogeneous across domains.

contributions.claim: AnomalyGFM is a graph foundation model for graph anomaly detection that supports zero-shot inference and few-shot prompt tuning across diverse graph datasets.
The model aligns learnable, data-independent normal and abnormal class prototypes with node representation residuals to obtain graph-agnostic abnormality representations.
Few-shot prompt tuning uses labeled normal nodes from a new graph for adaptation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly propose AnomalyGFM as a graph anomaly detection-oriented graph foundation model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on 11 widely used graph anomaly detection datasets with real anomalies, covering social, finance, and co-review networks, reportedly show that AnomalyGFM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art competing methods in both zero-shot and few-shot settings.
The authors report that the method supports zero-shot graph anomaly detection on new graphs, including very large-scale graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph anomaly detection seeks to identify abnormal nodes.
Generalist graph models have difficulty learning transferable representations for cross-domain anomaly patterns.
AnomalyGFM uses residual features and graph-agnostic normal and abnormal prototypes for zero-shot inference and few-shot prompt tuning.
The authors report favorable results across 11 real-anomaly datasets and both evaluation settings.

source_observation.claim: The method projects node information into a unified feature space using representation residuals relative to neighboring nodes.

interpretation.claim: Comparing local deviations in a shared representation space may help transfer anomaly detection across graphs with different structures or domains.

application.claim: For cross-domain graph anomaly detection, consider learning transferable representations centered on deviations from local context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy works beyond the reported graph domains, datasets, or anomaly types.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the pre-training data, model architecture, optimization procedure, or prompt-tuning details.
The abstract does not provide dataset-level metrics, baselines, statistical testing, or computational costs.
The abstract does not clarify the availability, license, or reproducibility of the reported code.
